newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco posts loss in quarter, hurt by charges.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco posts loss in quarter, hurt by charges.

text.p: Tenneco Inc. Monday reported a loss for the fourth quarter and a sharp drop in profits for the year, reflecting restructuring and other charges as it overhauled its line of businesses.
But Greenwich, Conn.-based Tenneco said its ongoing businesses, automotive parts and speciality packaging, had strong operating earnings for the full year.
Greenwich, Conn.-based Tenneco had a net loss of $361 million, or $2.15 a share, in the quarter, compared with a net profit of $183 million, or $1.05 a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Sales rose 22 percent to $1.69 billion from $1.38 billion.

The results included a one-time loss of $235 million from early retirement of debt and a loss of $90 million from the company's discontinued energy, shipbuilding and farm and construction equipment businesses.
For the year, operating income excluding special charges rose 25 percent to $313 million in automotive parts and nearly quadrupled to a record $237 million in speciality packaging.

"While the fourth quarter clearly demonstrates the promise and performance of the new Tenneco, it is also the period in which we recorded the costs for our transformation from a conglomerate into a focused global manufacturing company and for streamlining certain operations to enhance our competitiveness," Chairman Dana Mead said.
For the full year, net income fell to $410 million, or $2.33 a share, from $735 million, or $4.16 a share, in 1995. Revenues rose to $6.57 billion from $5.22 billion.
Results for 1995 were restated to reflect the changes in Tenneco as of December 1996.
